newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deng voiced remorse over Tiananmen -- agency.
newsitem.headline: Deng voiced remorse over Tiananmen -- agency.

text.p: China's late leader Deng Xiaoping voiced remorse over the 1989 Tiananmen Square military crackdown before he died last month, Japan's Kyodo news agency said on Tuesday.
The agency quoted Chinese sources as saying a dying Deng called the military's action in firing on unarmed protesters on June 4, 1989, "the most regrettable event" in his life.
As head of the Central Military Commission at the time, Deng was instrumental in calling in the troops to end pro-democracy demonstrations in the square.
Many lives were lost in the crackdown but no precise figure is known.
Kyodo said Deng's last words consisted of just a few sentences.
Reviewing the achievements of his life, Deng said with pride: "All in all a lot of good things happened during my life."
He said Tiananmen was the most regrettable event in his life, and added: "We couldn't help at the time but take the most active response," the agency said.
It said the sources did not reveal to whom Deng was speaking or when.

A Chinese spokesman in Hong Kong last week denied a report that Deng had written a will apologising for the Tiananmen crackdown. The purported will, published in two Hong Kong newspapers, was a fabrication, it said.
